"""The last stage: an agent enters the calculated bid in the tender portal, signs it and reads the receipt.

The calculator has fixed every number. `submit_bid` hands them to a model as a bid sheet and lets it drive whatever
bid form the portal has: where the form is, what each step wants, which notation a field takes, how a position is
left out and when the signing code has to be requested are all read from the pages. A second agent, on the webmail,
fetches that code when the first one asks for it. Nothing here knows a field name or the order of the steps.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from decimal import Decimal

from browser_env import Tab
from calculator import Bid
from worker import ACTIONS_HELP, Agent

WRAP_UP = 150  # seconds before the deadline at which entering stops and signing starts: the code takes a while
MAIL_BUDGET = 120  # seconds one request to the mailbox may take
CLERK_STEPS, COURIER_STEPS = 120, 25
# Entering a bid is reading a form and copying values: without the model's long reasoning a turn takes about half
# the time, and the reply's "thought" still leaves it room to check a conversion.
CLERK_THINKS, COURIER_THINKS = False, False

CLERK = """You are the bid clerk of a manufacturer's sales engineering team. Your colleagues have researched a
public tender and a calculator has priced it: the BID SHEET below is the final result. You work the tender portal
"{site}" at {url} in your own browser tab, and your whole job is to get exactly this bid into the portal's bid
form, sign it, submit it and read the confirmation. You do not research and you do not recalculate.

TASK BRIEF (background on what a valid submission is; the values to enter come from the bid sheet)
{brief}
END OF BRIEF

BIDDER
{bidder}

BID SHEET
{sheet}

Reading the bid sheet
- "decision" is "bid" or "no_bid". A no_bid has no positions and a total of zero: take the form's way of
  declining, and still sign and submit it.
- "positions" has one entry per tender position that is offered. Enter each under its own position number.
- "material" describes the offered product, for forms that make you pick or configure it: choose what equals
  these values.
- Amounts are net EUR, written here with a decimal point and without thousands separators. A field may expect
  another notation (a decimal comma, a unit, whole numbers for weeks and pieces): follow its hints, placeholder
  and error messages. Change the notation only, never the value.
- null means the value is not known: leave that field empty. 0 or 0.00 is a known zero: enter it.
- "omitted_positions" could not be priced. Never invent values for them: use the form's explicit way of leaving
  a position out, if it has one.

{actions}
One more action:
  {{"do": "ask_mail", "task": "<what you need and how to recognise it>"}}
      A colleague who has the bidder's mailbox open in another browser looks for it and answers. This is how you
      get the signing code (TAN) the portal sends by mail. Ask only after you have triggered the code in the
      portal, and pass on what you know about it (the tender reference, that you requested it just now, anything
      the portal displayed about it): the mailbox also holds older codes that no longer work.

How to work
- Start from the page you are on and find the bid form of tender {reference}. Log in again if the portal asks.
- A bid form asks, in an order of its own, for things like the bidder's details, bid or no bid, the positions,
  the commercial terms, declarations, a review and a signature. Read each page and give it what it asks for,
  from the bidder data and the bid sheet. Fill every field the sheet has a value for, optional ones included.
- Read the form's own instructions: when entries are saved, what going back does, which fields are required.
  Do the fields of a page in one reply, then the control that saves them or moves on.
- After each step look at the result. If the form reports an error or did not keep a value, correct that field
  before you move on.
- Declarations: read what each one says. Give the confirmations a valid bid needs; leave unticked, or untick,
  options that would alter the bid or have nothing to do with it.
- On the review page compare what the form lists with the bid sheet: reference, decision, every position, the
  discount and the total. Go back and correct differences while there is time.
- Signing: trigger the code in the portal, get it with ask_mail, enter it and submit. A submission is final.
  If the portal rejects a code, request a fresh one instead of trying the same again.
- You are finished only when the portal confirms that the bid was received. Then finish with done and put the
  confirmation (its receipt number or code, else its wording) in "answer". If you cannot submit, finish with
  done without "answer" and say why in "summary".
- Watch the time. A bid that is entered but not submitted scores nothing; a submitted bid with positions left
  out keeps the points of the positions it holds. When the head of a turn says time is short, do as it says.
"""

COURIER = """You have the sales mailbox of a bidding company open in the webmail "{site}" at {url}, in your own
browser tab. A colleague is entering the company's bid for tender {reference} in the tender portal right now and
asks you for something from the mailbox, usually the one-time signing code (TAN) the portal has just mailed.

{actions}

How to work
- The request heads every turn, together with the answers you gave earlier in this run.
- Codes expire. The mailbox can hold older codes, codes for other tenders whose references look alike, and
  unrelated mail with similar subjects. The one that counts is the newest message that matches the request. Open
  the message itself and check its reference and time before you answer: a row in a list is not enough.
- Lists can be paged, sorted either way and split over folders, and new mail may only show after a reload. If the
  message is not there yet, reload and look again a few times.
- Log in again if the webmail asks.
- Finish with done and put ONLY the value asked for in "answer": a code exactly as written, nothing around it.
  If you cannot find it, finish with done without "answer" and say in "summary" what you saw instead.
"""


def _amount(value: Decimal | None) -> str | None:
    return None if value is None else f"{value:.2f}"


def bid_sheet(bid: Bid) -> dict:
    """The bid as the clerk gets it: the answer's fields with exact amounts as text, the positions left out, and per
    position the offered material's attributes for forms that have the bidder configure the product."""
    positions = []
    for line in bid.lines:
        material = line.material
        positions.append({
            "position": line.position, "material_number": line.material_number,
            "material": None if material is None else {
                "bore_mm": material.bore_mm, "stroke_mm": material.stroke_mm, "pressure_bar": material.pressure_bar,
                "mounting": material.mounting, "certification": material.certification},
            "quantity": line.quantity, "unit_price": _amount(line.unit_price),
            "lead_time_weeks": line.lead_time_weeks, "base_unit_price": _amount(line.base_unit_price),
            "surcharge_per_unit": _amount(line.surcharge_per_unit),
            "packaging_per_unit": _amount(line.packaging_per_unit), "rebate_total": _amount(line.rebate_total)})
    discount = Decimal(bid.discount_percent)
    return {"tender_reference": bid.tender_reference, "decision": bid.decision, "currency": "EUR",
            "discount_percent": int(discount) if discount == discount.to_integral_value() else float(discount),
            "positions": positions, "omitted_positions": list(bid.omitted), "total_net": _amount(bid.total_net)}


async def submit_bid(tender_tab: Tab, mail_tab: Tab | None, bid: Bid, context: dict, brief: str,
                     deadline: float) -> dict:
    """Have an agent enter, sign and submit `bid` in the tender portal before `deadline` (a time.time() value).

    `context` holds tender_reference, scenario_date, company, vat_id and email. Returns {"submitted", "receipt",
    "notes"}: `receipt` is the portal's confirmation as the agent read it, empty when there was none.
    """
    reference = str(context.get("tender_reference") or bid.tender_reference)
    codes: list[str] = []  # what the mailbox handed out so far: a used code must not be handed out again

    async def ask_mail(action: dict) -> str:
        task = str(action.get("task") or "").strip()
        if not task:
            return 'ask_mail needs a "task": say what you need from the mailbox and how to recognise it'
        if mail_tab is None:
            return "there is no mailbox in this run, so nothing can be fetched by mail"

        def request() -> str:
            text = f"REQUEST FROM YOUR COLLEAGUE AT THE TENDER PORTAL\n{task}"
            if codes:
                text += ("\n\nANSWERS YOU GAVE EARLIER IN THIS RUN (they are used up: a new request needs a newer "
                         "message)\n" + "\n".join(f"- {code}" for code in codes))
            return text

        system = COURIER.format(site=mail_tab.site_id, url=mail_tab.base_url, reference=reference,
                                actions=ACTIONS_HELP)
        courier = Agent("courier", mail_tab, system, request, deadline=min(deadline, time.time() + MAIL_BUDGET),
                        max_steps=COURIER_STEPS, think=COURIER_THINKS)
        outcome = await courier.run()
        answer = str(outcome.get("answer") or "").strip()
        if not answer:
            return "the mailbox colleague found nothing: " + (outcome.get("summary") or "no result in the time given")
        codes.append(answer)
        return f'the mailbox colleague answers: "{answer}"' + (f' ({outcome["summary"]})' if outcome.get("summary") else "")

    def heading() -> str:
        left = int(deadline - time.time())
        text = f"YOUR JOB: enter, sign and submit the bid for tender {reference}, then read the confirmation."
        if codes:
            text += "\nCodes from the mailbox so far, oldest first: " + ", ".join(codes)
        if left < WRAP_UP:
            text += (f"\nTIME IS SHORT ({left} s). Enter no further positions: leave out the ones not entered yet if "
                     "the form allows it, go straight to the signature, fetch the code and submit what is entered.")
        return text

    bidder = {"company": context.get("company"), "vat_id": context.get("vat_id"), "email": context.get("email")}
    system = CLERK.format(site=tender_tab.site_id, url=tender_tab.base_url, brief=brief, reference=reference,
                          bidder=json.dumps(bidder, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1),
                          sheet=json.dumps(bid_sheet(bid), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), actions=ACTIONS_HELP)
    clerk = Agent("submit", tender_tab, system, heading, extra={"ask_mail": ask_mail}, deadline=deadline,
                  max_steps=CLERK_STEPS, think=CLERK_THINKS)
    outcome = await clerk.run()
    receipt = str(outcome.get("answer") or "").strip()
    notes = str(outcome.get("summary") or "")
    if not outcome.get("done"):
        notes = (notes + " " if notes else "") + f"stopped after {outcome.get('steps', 0)} steps without a confirmation"
    return {"submitted": bool(outcome.get("done") and receipt), "receipt": receipt, "notes": notes}

"""Deterministic bid arithmetic for the RFQ-to-bid challenge.

The agents find and select the evidence; this module only applies the bid rules of the task brief to the structured
facts they filed: exact Decimal arithmetic, ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent, largest-remainder cent allocation, marginal
bonus bands, shared stock and delivery commitments. It contains no scenario values and never touches a website.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP
from fractions import Fraction

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
ZERO = Decimal("0")
HUNDRED = Decimal("100")

# Mass units to grams and index-rate units to EUR per gram, so any combination the sources use multiplies out.
MASS_TO_GRAMS = {"mg": Decimal("0.001"), "g": Decimal(1), "kg": Decimal(1000), "t": Decimal(1000000)}


def round_cents(value) -> Decimal:
    return Decimal(str(value)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def parse_number(raw, number_format: str | None = None) -> Decimal | None:
    """A number as written on a page ("1.234,56", "64,853 (en-US)", 12) as a Decimal; None when there is none.

    `number_format` is "de-DE" (decimal comma) or "en-US" (decimal point); an inline tag in `raw` wins. Without
    either, the separators decide, and a lone comma is read as a decimal comma, as German sources write it.
    """
    if raw is None or isinstance(raw, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(raw, Decimal):
        return raw
    if isinstance(raw, (int, float)):
        return Decimal(str(raw))
    text = str(raw).strip()
    tag = re.search(r"(de-DE|en-US)", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    fmt = (tag.group(1) if tag else number_format or "").lower()
    match = re.search(r"[-+]?\d[\d.,'\s  ]*", text)
    if not match:
        return None
    token = re.sub(r"['\s  ]", "", match.group(0)).rstrip(".,")
    try:
        if fmt == "en-us":
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if fmt == "de-de":
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
        if "," in token and "." in token:
            if token.rfind(",") > token.rfind("."):
                return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if "," in token:
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ".")) if token.count(",") == 1 else Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if token.count(".") > 1:
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", ""))
        return Decimal(token)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def parse_when(raw, end_of_day: bool = False) -> datetime | None:
    """An ISO 8601 date or timestamp (as the extraction step writes them) as an aware UTC datetime.

    A value without a time is a whole day: its start, or its last microsecond with `end_of_day`, so that validity
    periods include both endpoints.
    """
    if not raw:
        return None
    text = str(raw).strip()
    try:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text):
            day = datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return day + timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1) if end_of_day else day
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        german = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\.(\d{4})(?:[,\s]+(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}))?", text)
        if not german:
            return None
        day, month, year, hour, minute = german.groups()
        try:
            when = datetime(int(year), int(month), int(day), int(hour or 0), int(minute or 0))
        except ValueError:
            return None
        if hour is None and end_of_day:
            when += timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1)
    return when.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if when.tzinfo is None else when.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def allocate_cents(total_cents: int, weights: dict[str, Decimal], method: str = "largest_remainder") -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Split `total_cents` across the keys in proportion to `weights`, as EUR amounts that sum exactly.

    Every share is floored to the cent; the cents left over go out by `method`: "largest_remainder" (ties to the
    lower key), "remainder_to_first", "remainder_to_last" or "remainder_to_largest" (the biggest weight).
    """
    keys = sorted(weights, key=position_order)
    total_weight = sum(weights.values(), ZERO)
    if not keys or total_cents <= 0 or total_weight <= 0:
        return {key: ZERO for key in keys}
    # Exact fractions: a tie between remainders must be a tie, not a matter of decimal precision.
    exact = {key: Fraction(total_cents) * Fraction(weights[key]) / Fraction(total_weight) for key in keys}
    cents = {key: math.floor(exact[key]) for key in keys}
    left = total_cents - sum(cents.values())
    if method == "remainder_to_first":
        cents[keys[0]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_last":
        cents[keys[-1]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_largest":
        cents[max(keys, key=lambda key: (weights[key], -keys.index(key)))] += left
    else:
        for key in sorted(keys, key=lambda key: (-(exact[key] - cents[key]), keys.index(key)))[:left]:
            cents[key] += 1
    return {key: Decimal(cents[key]) * CENT for key in keys}


def position_order(key) -> list:
    """Position identifiers in ascending order: their numbers count as numbers ("2" before "10")."""
    return [(0, int(part), "") if part.isdigit() else (1, 0, part) for part in re.findall(r"\d+|\D+", str(key))]


def same_text(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Two attribute values name the same thing: case, spacing and punctuation aside."""
    def norm(value):
        return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zäöüß]+", "", (value or "").lower())
    return norm(a) == norm(b)


NO_CERTIFICATE = ("", "-", "keine", "kein", "ohne", "none", "no", "n/a", "na", "nicht gefordert", "keine gefordert",
                  "nicht erforderlich", "keine erforderlich", "entfällt")


def same_certification(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Certifications match, with every way of writing "none required" counting as the same."""
    def norm(value):
        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (value or "").strip().lower()).strip(" .—–")
        return "" if text in NO_CERTIFICATE else text
    return same_text(norm(a), norm(b))


@dataclass
class Position:
    position: str
    requirement_ref: str
    quantity: int
    is_set: bool = False  # the quantity counts sets, not pieces
    description: str = ""


@dataclass
class Clarification:
    """One answer of the tender's Q&A, as far as it changes the bid."""
    number: str
    when: datetime | None
    withdraws: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    quantity_changes: list[tuple[str, int, bool | None]] = field(default_factory=list)  # position, quantity, is_set
    amendments: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)  # revision, requirement, attribute, value
    assignments: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # position -> {kind: key}
    setup_fees: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)  # position -> ordinary setup fee, EUR


@dataclass

---README---
# QuoteCraft — from RFQ to bid

A team of model-directed agents that reads a tender across four business websites it has never seen, works out the
bid the rules call for, and enters and signs it in the tender portal.

## How it works

```
task brief ──► model reads it: tender, scenario date, authorized senders
                    │
   ┌────────────────┼──────────────────┬─────────────────┐
   ▼                ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 agent            agent              agent             agent        one per website, each in its own browser:
 tender portal    supplier portal    ERP               webmail      the model picks every click, search and page
   │  keep          │  keep            │  keep           │  keep
   └────────────────┴───────┬──────────┴─────────────────┘
                            ▼
                     shared case file        a model call turns each filed page into typed facts;
                            │                the brief's rules yield the open questions all agents see
                            ▼
                      calculator.py          the bid rules as exact Decimal arithmetic
                            ▼
                     submission agent        fills the bid form it finds; the mail agent fetches the TAN
```

1. **Read the brief.** One model call extracts the tender reference, the scenario date, the bidder and which
   mailbox the rules authorize for which kind of record.
2. **Investigate in parallel.** One agent per website (`worker.Agent`). Each turn it sees its page as accessible
   text with numbered controls (`browser_env.Tab`), plus the case file and its open questions, and answers with
   actions: log in, click, fill, select, search, page through a list, download a file, or `keep` the page as
   evidence. Nothing in the code knows a URL, a selector or a click path of any website.
3. **File facts.** `keep` hands the page to a second model call that extracts typed records (positions, Q&A
   answers, revisions, requirements, materials, price conditions, mail records). `casefile.CaseFile` merges them
   and derives what is still unknown: a catalogue group found in the specification becomes an ERP question, a key
   in a Q&A answer becomes a mailbox question, and so on. Agents finish when their website has nothing left to add.
4. **Calculate.** `calculator.calculate_bid` applies the bid rules of the brief: latest clarification, withdrawn
   answers, scoped amendments, usable travel, sets to pieces, price scales, FX, conditional discount, condition
   clauses, shared stock, delivery commitments, cartons, pooled setup, project bonus, rounding. A position that
   lacks evidence is left out rather than guessed.
5. **Submit.** `submit.submit_bid` gives the bid to an agent on the tender portal, which fills whatever bid form
   it finds, asks a mail agent for the signing TAN and confirms the receipt.

## What is model and what is code

| The model decides | Code does |
| --- | --- |
| where to go, what to search for, which record or document matters | renders the page, carries out the chosen action |
| how to pass a popup, access check, login or error page | retries a server error, re-reads the page |
| which page is evidence and of what kind | pages through a list the model chose, reads a file it chose |
| what a page says (extraction into typed facts) | parses numbers and dates, checks sender, reference and date |
| when a search is complete or a record does not exist | arithmetic, rounding, allocation |
| how to fill and sign the bid form | — |

No scenario value (reference, material, price, key, login, TAN) appears anywhere in the package.

## Files

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Entry point: reads the run, starts the site agents, calculates, hands the bid to the submission agent |
| `worker.py` | The agent loop: page text in, the model's actions out |
| `browser_env.py` | A tab as accessible text (labels, descriptions, tooltips, frames, collapsed sections) and the actions on it |
| `casefile.py` | Evidence to typed facts, open questions, calculator inputs |
| `calculator.py` | The bid rules as Decimal arithmetic |
| `submit.py` | Bid entry and signing |
| `llm.py` | The hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy: JSON replies, retries, a concurrency cap |
| `run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py` | The starter kit's plumbing: the run contract, the run's browsers, the hosted models |
| `agent.json` | Setup (`uv sync`), run command, four browsers, the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The calculator rule by rule, the page rendering against local fixtures, the plumbing against fakes |

## Running it

In the sandbox the platform sets everything (`CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`, `CDP_URLS`, `QWEN_*`):

```sh
atira test-run . --challenge rfq
```

On your machine, against the public websites with the scouting logins (nothing counts), with `atira models proxy`
running in another terminal:

```sh
python ../tools/local_run.py --no-submit
```

Switches: `AGENT_SKIP_SUBMIT=1` stops before the bid form, `AGENT_SITES=a,b` starts only those site agents,
`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` caps an agent's turns, `AGENT_DUMP=<file>` writes the case file as JSON.

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover tests
```

1. The model reads the brief: which tender, which date, which senders the rules authorize.
2. One agent per website explores it in its own browser. Each decides where to go, what to search for and which
   pages are evidence, and files those pages. A model call turns every filed page into structured facts in the

   fact found on one website (a catalogue group, a key) steers the search on another.
3. `calculator.py` applies the bid rules to the facts: arithmetic only.

INVESTIGATOR = """You are one of several research agents preparing a tender bid for a manufacturer's sales
engineering team. Each agent works a different website at the same time; you work the website "{site}" at {url}
in your own browser tab. Together you must find every fact the bid rules need. You only find and file evidence:
you never calculate prices.

TASK BRIEF (the rules are authoritative)
{brief}
END OF BRIEF

{actions}
Case-file actions:
  {{"do": "keep", "kind": "<kind>", "note": "<what it is>"}}
      File the document in front of you (the current page, or the document you just collected or fetched) as
      evidence. Its facts are then extracted into the shared case file and reported back to you. Kinds:
        positions         the tender's bill of quantities
        clarifications    answers of the tender's bidder Q&A
        revisions         the revision history of the buyer's technical specification
        requirements      the requirement details of one specification revision
        material          ERP master data of materials: technical attributes, status, planning, stock
        price_conditions  ERP price conditions of one material: validity, currency, quantity scales
        mail              an opened mail message
  {{"do": "answer", "question": "<id>", "status": "complete" | "absent", "note": "..."}}
      Close an open question: "complete" when all its evidence is filed (needed for lists that only you know to be
      complete), "absent" when you searched properly and what is asked for does not exist.

How to work
- Every turn starts with the case file and the OPEN QUESTIONS. Work on the questions your website can answer;
  the other agents handle the rest. Facts they file show up in the case file and can open new questions for you.
- You remember only the page in front of you: file a relevant page with keep BEFORE you leave it. keep files the
  whole document, also what was cut from your view. File a document once, with the right kind.
- File pages that state the facts themselves (an opened document, record or message), not menus or hit lists.
  For a paged list or document that matters, use collect so that no page is missed, then keep it.
- The websites hold traps: superseded revisions, look-alike records for other tender references, drafts and
  previews, blocked materials, future-dated records, values in the wrong unit or number format. Check dates,
  references, senders and status marks before you rely on a record, and follow the brief's rules on which one
  counts. When in doubt, file both and let the facts decide.
- Follow the search hints a website gives. If a search returns nothing or too much, change the search terms.
- When no open question is left that your website can answer right now, finish with done, also when you need
  facts the other agents have not filed yet. You are called again as soon as the case file brings new questions.
  Never idle with wait and never browse around to pass the time.
"""


class Team:
    """Holds an agent that has nothing to do until the case file brings news, and ends the investigation when every
    agent is idle and no filed document is still being read."""

    def __init__(self, case: CaseFile, names: list[str], deadline: float):
        self.case, self.names, self.deadline = case, set(names), deadline
        self.idle: set[str] = set()
        self.finished = asyncio.Event()

    def hook(self, name: str):
        async def hold(why: str) -> str | None:
            version = self.case.version
            before = {qid for qid, _ in self.case.questions()}
            self.idle.add(name)
            try:
                while not self.finished.is_set() and time.time() < self.deadline:
                    changed = await self.case.wait_change(version, 1.0)
                    if self.finished.is_set():
                        break
                    if changed:
                        version = self.case.version
                        fresh = {qid for qid, _ in self.case.questions()} - before
                        if fresh or self.case.news.get(name):
                            return "The case file has news" + (f"; new open questions: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}" if fresh else "") + "."
                    elif self.idle == self.names and self.case.pending == 0:
                        self.finished.set()
                return None
            finally:
                self.idle.discard(name)
        return hold

def _amount(value: Decimal | None) -> str | None:
    return None if value is None else f"{value:.2f}"


def bid_sheet(bid: Bid) -> dict:
    """The bid as the clerk gets it: the answer's fields with exact amounts as text, the positions left out, and per
    position the offered material's attributes for forms that have the bidder configure the product."""
    positions = []
    for line in bid.lines:
        material = line.material
        positions.append({
            "position": line.position, "material_number": line.material_number,
            "material": None if material is None else {
                "bore_mm": material.bore_mm, "stroke_mm": material.stroke_mm, "pressure_bar": material.pressure_bar,
                "mounting": material.mounting, "certification": material.certification},
            "quantity": line.quantity, "unit_price": _amount(line.unit_price),
            "lead_time_weeks": line.lead_time_weeks, "base_unit_price": _amount(line.base_unit_price),
            "surcharge_per_unit": _amount(line.surcharge_per_unit),
            "packaging_per_unit": _amount(line.packaging_per_unit), "rebate_total": _amount(line.rebate_total)})
    discount = Decimal(bid.discount_percent)
    return {"tender_reference": bid.tender_reference, "decision": bid.decision, "currency": "EUR",

                     deadline: float) -> dict:
    """Have an agent enter, sign and submit `bid` in the tender portal before `deadline` (a time.time() value).

    reference = str(context.get("tender_reference") or bid.tender_reference)
    codes: list[str] = []  # what the mailbox handed out so far: a used code must not be handed out again

    async def ask_mail(action: dict) -> str:

        if mail_tab is None:
            return "there is no mailbox in this run, so nothing can be fetched by mail"

        def request() -> str:
            text = f"REQUEST FROM YOUR COLLEAGUE AT THE TENDER PORTAL\n{task}"
            if codes:
                text += ("\n\nANSWERS YOU GAVE EARLIER IN THIS RUN (they are used up: a new request needs a newer "
                         "message)\n" + "\n".join(f"- {code}" for code in codes))
            return text

        system = COURIER.format(site=mail_tab.site_id, url=mail_tab.base_url, reference=reference,
                                actions=ACTIONS_HELP)
        courier = Agent("courier", mail_tab, system, request, deadline=min(deadline, time.time() + MAIL_BUDGET),
                        max_steps=COURIER_STEPS, think=COURIER_THINKS)
        outcome = await courier.run()
        answer = str(outcome.get("answer") or "").strip()
        if not answer:
            return "the mailbox colleague found nothing: " + (outcome.get("summary") or "no result in the time given")
        codes.append(answer)
        return f'the mailbox colleague answers: "{answer}"' + (f' ({outcome["summary"]})' if outcome.get("summary") else "")

    def heading() -> str:
        left = int(deadline - time.time())
        text = f"YOUR JOB: enter, sign and submit the bid for tender {reference}, then read the confirmation."
        if codes:
            text += "\nCodes from the mailbox so far, oldest first: " + ", ".join(codes)
        if left < WRAP_UP:
            text += (f"\nTIME IS SHORT ({left} s). Enter no further positions: leave out the ones not entered yet if "
                     "the form allows it, go straight to the signature, fetch the code and submit what is entered.")
        return text

    bidder = {"company": context.get("company"), "vat_id": context.get("vat_id"), "email": context.get("email")}
    system = CLERK.format(site=tender_tab.site_id, url=tender_tab.base_url, brief=brief, reference=reference,
                          bidder=json.dumps(bidder, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1),
                          sheet=json.dumps(bid_sheet(bid), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), actions=ACTIONS_HELP)
    clerk = Agent("submit", tender_tab, system, heading, extra={"ask_mail": ask_mail}, deadline=deadline,
                  max_steps=CLERK_STEPS, think=CLERK_THINKS)
    outcome = await clerk.run()
    receipt = str(outcome.get("answer") or "").strip()
    notes = str(outcome.get("summary") or "")
    if not outcome.get("done"):
        notes = (notes + " " if notes else "") + f"stopped after {outcome.get('steps', 0)} steps without a confirmation"
    return {"submitted": bool(outcome.get("done") and receipt), "receipt": receipt, "notes": notes}

"""Deterministic bid arithmetic for the RFQ-to-bid challenge.

The agents find and select the evidence; this module only applies the bid rules of the task brief to the structured
facts they filed: exact Decimal arithmetic, ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent, largest-remainder cent allocation, marginal
bonus bands, shared stock and delivery commitments. It contains no scenario values and never touches a website.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP
from fractions import Fraction

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
ZERO = Decimal("0")
HUNDRED = Decimal("100")

# Mass units to grams and index-rate units to EUR per gram, so any combination the sources use multiplies out.
MASS_TO_GRAMS = {"mg": Decimal("0.001"), "g": Decimal(1), "kg": Decimal(1000), "t": Decimal(1000000)}


def round_cents(value) -> Decimal:
    return Decimal(str(value)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def parse_number(raw, number_format: str | None = None) -> Decimal | None:
    """A number as written on a page ("1.234,56", "64,853 (en-US)", 12) as a Decimal; None when there is none.

    `number_format` is "de-DE" (decimal comma) or "en-US" (decimal point); an inline tag in `raw` wins. Without
    either, the separators decide, and a lone comma is read as a decimal comma, as German sources write it.
    """
    if raw is None or isinstance(raw, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(raw, Decimal):
        return raw
    if isinstance(raw, (int, float)):
        return Decimal(str(raw))
    text = str(raw).strip()
    tag = re.search(r"(de-DE|en-US)", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    fmt = (tag.group(1) if tag else number_format or "").lower()
    match = re.search(r"[-+]?\d[\d.,'\s  ]*", text)
    if not match:
        return None
    token = re.sub(r"['\s  ]", "", match.group(0)).rstrip(".,")
    try:
        if fmt == "en-us":
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if fmt == "de-de":
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
        if "," in token and "." in token:
            if token.rfind(",") > token.rfind("."):
                return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if "," in token:
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ".")) if token.count(",") == 1 else Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if token.count(".") > 1:
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", ""))
        return Decimal(token)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def parse_when(raw, end_of_day: bool = False) -> datetime | None:
    """An ISO 8601 date or timestamp (as the extraction step writes them) as an aware UTC datetime.

    A value without a time is a whole day: its start, or its last microsecond with `end_of_day`, so that validity
    periods include both endpoints.
    """
    if not raw:
        return None
    text = str(raw).strip()
    try:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text):
            day = datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return day + timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1) if end_of_day else day
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        german = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\.(\d{4})(?:[,\s]+(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}))?", text)
        if not german:
            return None
        day, month, year, hour, minute = german.groups()
        try:
            when = datetime(int(year), int(month), int(day), int(hour or 0), int(minute or 0))
        except ValueError:
            return None
        if hour is None and end_of_day:
            when += timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1)
    return when.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if when.tzinfo is None else when.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def allocate_cents(total_cents: int, weights: dict[str, Decimal], method: str = "largest_remainder") -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Split `total_cents` across the keys in proportion to `weights`, as EUR amounts that sum exactly.

    Every share is floored to the cent; the cents left over go out by `method`: "largest_remainder" (ties to the
    lower key), "remainder_to_first", "remainder_to_last" or "remainder_to_largest" (the biggest weight).
    """
    keys = sorted(weights, key=position_order)
    total_weight = sum(weights.values(), ZERO)
    if not keys or total_cents <= 0 or total_weight <= 0:
        return {key: ZERO for key in keys}
    # Exact fractions: a tie between remainders must be a tie, not a matter of decimal precision.
    exact = {key: Fraction(total_cents) * Fraction(weights[key]) / Fraction(total_weight) for key in keys}
    cents = {key: math.floor(exact[key]) for key in keys}
    left = total_cents - sum(cents.values())
    if method == "remainder_to_first":
        cents[keys[0]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_last":
        cents[keys[-1]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_largest":
        cents[max(keys, key=lambda key: (weights[key], -keys.index(key)))] += left
    else:
        for key in sorted(keys, key=lambda key: (-(exact[key] - cents[key]), keys.index(key)))[:left]:
            cents[key] += 1
    return {key: Decimal(cents[key]) * CENT for key in keys}


def position_order(key) -> list:
    """Position identifiers in ascending order: their numbers count as numbers ("2" before "10")."""
    return [(0, int(part), "") if part.isdigit() else (1, 0, part) for part in re.findall(r"\d+|\D+", str(key))]


def same_text(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Two attribute values name the same thing: case, spacing and punctuation aside."""
    def norm(value):
        return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zäöüß]+", "", (value or "").lower())
    return norm(a) == norm(b)


NO_CERTIFICATE = ("", "-", "keine", "kein", "ohne", "none", "no", "n/a", "na", "nicht gefordert", "keine gefordert",
                  "nicht erforderlich", "keine erforderlich", "entfällt")


def same_certification(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Certifications match, with every way of writing "none required" counting as the same."""
    def norm(value):
        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (value or "").strip().lower()).strip(" .—–")
        return "" if text in NO_CERTIFICATE else text
    return same_text(norm(a), norm(b))


@dataclass
class Position:
    position: str
    requirement_ref: str
    quantity: int
    is_set: bool = False  # the quantity counts sets, not pieces
    description: str = ""

    stroke_mm: int | None = None

    mounting: str | None = None

class PriceCondition:

    valid_to: datetime | None

    catalogue_group: str | None = None

    pressure_bar: int | None = None

# QuoteCraft — from RFQ to bid

A team of model-directed agents that reads a tender across four business websites it has never seen, works out the
bid the rules call for, and enters and signs it in the tender portal.

## How it works

```
task brief ──► model reads it: tender, scenario date, authorized senders
                    │
   ┌────────────────┼──────────────────┬─────────────────┐
   ▼                ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 agent            agent              agent             agent        one per website, each in its own browser:
 tender portal    supplier portal    ERP               webmail      the model picks every click, search and page
   │  keep          │  keep            │  keep           │  keep
   └────────────────┴───────┬──────────┴─────────────────┘
                            ▼
                     shared case file        a model call turns each filed page into typed facts;
                            │                the brief's rules yield the open questions all agents see
                            ▼
                      calculator.py          the bid rules as exact Decimal arithmetic
                            ▼
                     submission agent        fills the bid form it finds; the mail agent fetches the TAN
```

1. **Read the brief.** One model call extracts the tender reference, the scenario date, the bidder and which
   mailbox the rules authorize for which kind of record.
2. **Investigate in parallel.** One agent per website (`worker.Agent`). Each turn it sees its page as accessible
   text with numbered controls (`browser_env.Tab`), plus the case file and its open questions, and answers with
   actions: log in, click, fill, select, search, page through a list, download a file, or `keep` the page as
   evidence. Nothing in the code knows a URL, a selector or a click path of any website.
3. **File facts.** `keep` hands the page to a second model call that extracts typed records (positions, Q&A
   answers, revisions, requirements, materials, price conditions, mail records). `casefile.CaseFile` merges them
   and derives what is still unknown: a catalogue group found in the specification becomes an ERP question, a key
   in a Q&A answer becomes a mailbox question, and so on. Agents finish when their website has nothing left to add.
4. **Calculate.** `calculator.calculate_bid` applies the bid rules of the brief: latest clarification, withdrawn
   answers, scoped amendments, usable travel, sets to pieces, price scales, FX, conditional discount, condition
   clauses, shared stock, delivery commitments, cartons, pooled setup, project bonus, rounding. A position that
   lacks evidence is left out rather than guessed.
5. **Submit.** `submit.submit_bid` gives the bid to an agent on the tender portal, which fills whatever bid form
   it finds, asks a mail agent for the signing TAN and confirms the receipt.

## What is model and what is code

| The model decides | Code does |
| --- | --- |
| where to go, what to search for, which record or document matters | renders the page, carries out the chosen action |
| how to pass a popup, access check, login or error page | retries a server error, re-reads the page |
| which page is evidence and of what kind | pages through a list the model chose, reads a file it chose |
| what a page says (extraction into typed facts) | parses numbers and dates, checks sender, reference and date |
| when a search is complete or a record does not exist | arithmetic, rounding, allocation |
| how to fill and sign the bid form | — |

No scenario value (reference, material, price, key, login, TAN) appears anywhere in the package.

## Files

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Entry point: reads the run, starts the site agents, calculates, hands the bid to the submission agent |
| `worker.py` | The agent loop: page text in, the model's actions out |
| `browser_env.py` | A tab as accessible text (labels, descriptions, tooltips, frames, collapsed sections) and the actions on it |
| `casefile.py` | Evidence to typed facts, open questions, calculator inputs |
| `calculator.py` | The bid rules as Decimal arithmetic |
| `submit.py` | Bid entry and signing |
| `llm.py` | The hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy: JSON replies, retries, a concurrency cap |
| `run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py` | The starter kit's plumbing: the run contract, the run's browsers, the hosted models |
| `agent.json` | Setup (`uv sync`), run command, four browsers, the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The calculator rule by rule, the page rendering against local fixtures, the plumbing against fakes |

## Running it

In the sandbox the platform sets everything (`CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`, `CDP_URLS`, `QWEN_*`):

```sh
atira test-run . --challenge rfq
```

On your machine, against the public websites with the scouting logins (nothing counts), with `atira models proxy`
running in another terminal:

```sh
python ../tools/local_run.py --no-submit
```

Switches: `AGENT_SKIP_SUBMIT=1` stops before the bid form, `AGENT_SITES=a,b` starts only those site agents,
`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` caps an agent's turns, `AGENT_DUMP=<file>` writes the case file as JSON.

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover tests
```

## What is implemented

- `starter-kit/agent.py` coordinates four site agents (tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, and mail) and keeps the
  navigation decisions model-directed at runtime.
- `worker.py`, `browser_env.py`, and `llm.py` provide accessible-page observations, bounded actions, downloads,

"""RFQ-to-bid: a team of model-directed agents, one per website, and a deterministic calculator.

1. The model reads the brief: which tender, which date, which senders the rules authorize.
2. One agent per website explores it in its own browser. Each decides where to go, what to search for and which
   pages are evidence, and files those pages. A model call turns every filed page into structured facts in the
   shared case file; the open questions derived from the brief's rules tell all agents what is still missing, so a
   fact found on one website (a catalogue group, a key) steers the search on another.
3. `calculator.py` applies the bid rules to the facts: arithmetic only.
4. An agent enters the bid in the tender portal, has the mail agent fetch the signing TAN, and submits.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import time

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import browsers
import llm

INVESTIGATOR = """You are one of several research agents preparing a tender bid for a manufacturer's sales
engineering team. Each agent works a different website at the same time; you work the website "{site}" at {url}
in your own browser tab. Together you must find every fact the bid rules need. You only find and file evidence:
you never calculate prices.

TASK BRIEF (the rules are authoritative)
{brief}
END OF BRIEF

{actions}
Case-file actions:
  {{"do": "keep", "kind": "<kind>", "note": "<what it is>"}}
      File the document in front of you (the current page, or the document you just collected or fetched) as
      evidence. Its facts are then extracted into the shared case file and reported back to you. Kinds:
        positions         the tender's bill of quantities
        clarifications    answers of the tender's bidder Q&A
        revisions         the revision history of the buyer's technical specification
        requirements      the requirement details of one specification revision
        material          ERP master data of materials: technical attributes, status, planning, stock
        price_conditions  ERP price conditions of one material: validity, currency, quantity scales
        mail              an opened mail message
  {{"do": "answer", "question": "<id>", "status": "complete" | "absent", "note": "..."}}
      Close an open question: "complete" when all its evidence is filed (needed for lists that only you know to be
      complete), "absent" when you searched properly and what is asked for does not exist.

How to work
- Every turn starts with the case file and the OPEN QUESTIONS. Work on the questions your website can answer;
  the other agents handle the rest. Facts they file show up in the case file and can open new questions for you.
- You remember only the page in front of you: file a relevant page with keep BEFORE you leave it. keep files the
  whole document, also what was cut from your view. File a document once, with the right kind.
- File pages that state the facts themselves (an opened document, record or message), not menus or hit lists.
  For a paged list or document that matters, use collect so that no page is missed, then keep it.
- The websites hold traps: superseded revisions, look-alike records for other tender references, drafts and
  previews, blocked materials, future-dated records, values in the wrong unit or number format. Check dates,
  references, senders and status marks before you rely on a record, and follow the brief's rules on which one
  counts. When in doubt, file both and let the facts decide.
- Follow the search hints a website gives. If a search returns nothing or too much, change the search terms.
- When no open question is left that your website can answer right now, finish with done, also when you need
  facts the other agents have not filed yet. You are called again as soon as the case file brings new questions.
  Never idle with wait and never browse around to pass the time.
"""


class Team:
    """Holds an agent that has nothing to do until the case file brings news, and ends the investigation when every
    agent is idle and no filed document is still being read."""

    def __init__(self, case: CaseFile, names: list[str], deadline: float):
        self.case, self.names, self.deadline = case, set(names), deadline
        self.idle: set[str] = set()
        self.finished = asyncio.Event()

    def hook(self, name: str):
        async def hold(why: str) -> str | None:
            version = self.case.version
            before = {qid for qid, _ in self.case.questions()}
            self.idle.add(name)
            try:
                while not self.finished.is_set() and time.time() < self.deadline:
                    changed = await self.case.wait_change(version, 1.0)
                    if self.finished.is_set():
                        break
                    if changed:
                        version = self.case.version
                        fresh = {qid for qid, _ in self.case.questions()} - before
                        if fresh or self.case.news.get(name):
                            return "The case file has news" + (f"; new open questions: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}" if fresh else "") + "."
                    elif self.idle == self.names and self.case.pending == 0:
                        self.finished.set()
                return None
            finally:
                self.idle.discard(name)
        return hold


def investigator(case: CaseFile, team: Team, tab: Tab, deadline: float) -> Agent:
    name = tab.site_id
    system = INVESTIGATOR.format(site=name, url=tab.base_url, brief=case.brief, actions=ACTIONS_HELP)

    def briefing() -> str:
        questions = case.questions()
        news = case.take_news(name)
        text = f"CASE FILE\n{case.status()}\n\nOPEN QUESTIONS\n"
        text += "\n".join(f"- [{qi…2284 tokens truncated…e it>"}}
      A colleague who has the bidder's mailbox open in another browser looks for it and answers. This is how you
      get the signing code (TAN) the portal sends by mail. Ask only after you have triggered the code in the
      portal, and pass on what you know about it (the tender reference, that you requested it just now, anything
      the portal displayed about it): the mailbox also holds older codes that no longer work.

How to work
- Start from the page you are on and find the bid form of tender {reference}. Log in again if the portal asks.
- A bid form asks, in an order of its own, for things like the bidder's details, bid or no bid, the positions,
  the commercial terms, declarations, a review and a signature. Read each page and give it what it asks for,
  from the bidder data and the bid sheet. Fill every field the sheet has a value for, optional ones included.
- Read the form's own instructions: when entries are saved, what going back does, which fields are required.
  Do the fields of a page in one reply, then the control that saves them or moves on.
- After each step look at the result. If the form reports an error or did not keep a value, correct that field
  before you move on.
- Declarations: read what each one says. Give the confirmations a valid bid needs; leave unticked, or untick,
  options that would alter the bid or have nothing to do with it.
- On the review page compare what the form lists with the bid sheet: reference, decision, every position, the
  discount and the total. Go back and correct differences while there is time.
- Signing: trigger the code in the portal, get it with ask_mail, enter it and submit. A submission is final.
  If the portal rejects a code, request a fresh one instead of trying the same again.
- You are finished only when the portal confirms that the bid was received. Then finish with done and put the
  confirmation (its receipt number or code, else its wording) in "answer". If you cannot submit, finish with
  done without "answer" and say why in "summary".
- Watch the time. A bid that is entered but not submitted scores nothing; a submitted bid with positions left
  out keeps the points of the positions it holds. When the head of a turn says time is short, do as it says.
"""

COURIER = """You have the sales mailbox of a bidding company open in the webmail "{site}" at {url}, in your own
browser tab. A colleague is entering the company's bid for tender {reference} in the tender portal right now and
asks you for something from the mailbox, usually the one-time signing code (TAN) the portal has just mailed.

{actions}

How to work
- The request heads every turn, together with the answers you gave earlier in this run.
- Codes expire. The mailbox can hold older codes, codes for other tenders whose references look alike, and
  unrelated mail with similar subjects. The one that counts is the newest message that matches the request. Open
  the message itself and check its reference and time before you answer: a row in a list is not enough.
- Lists can be paged, sorted either way and split over folders, and new mail may only show after a reload. If the
  message is not there yet, reload and look again a few times.
- Log in again if the webmail asks.
- Finish with done and put ONLY the value asked for in "answer": a code exactly as written, nothing around it.
  If you cannot find it, finish with done without "answer" and say in "summary" what you saw instead.
"""


def _amount(value: Decimal | None) -> str | None:
    return None if value is None else f"{value:.2f}"


def bid_sheet(bid: Bid) -> dict:
    """The bid as the clerk gets it: the answer's fields with exact amounts as text, the positions left out, and per
    position the offered material's attributes for forms that have the bidder configure the product."""
    positions = []
    for line in bid.lines:
        material = line.material
        positions.append({
            "position": line.position, "material_number": line.material_number,
            "material": None if material is None else {
                "bore_mm": material.bore_mm, "stroke_mm": material.stroke_mm, "pressure_bar": material.pressure_bar,
                "mounting": material.mounting, "certification": material.certification},
            "quantity": line.quantity, "unit_price": _amount(line.unit_price),
            "lead_time_weeks": line.lead_time_weeks, "base_unit_price": _amount(line.base_unit_price),
            "surcharge_per_unit": _amount(line.surcharge_per_unit),
            "packaging_per_unit": _amount(line.packaging_per_unit), "rebate_total": _amount(line.rebate_total)})
    discount = Decimal(bid.discount_percent)
    return {"tender_reference": bid.tender_reference, "decision": bid.decision, "currency": "EUR",
            "discount_percent": int(discount) if discount == discount.to_integral_value() else float(discount),
            "positions": positions, "omitted_positions": list(bid.omitted), "total_net": _amount(bid.total_net)}


async def submit_bid(tender_tab: Tab, mail_tab: Tab | None, bid: Bid, context: dict, brief: str,
                     deadline: float) -> dict:
    """Have an agent enter, sign and submit `bid` in the tender portal before `deadline` (a time.time() value).

    `context` holds tender_reference, scenario_date, company, vat_id and email. Returns {"submitted", "receipt",
    "notes"}: `receipt` is the portal's confirmation as the agent read it, empty when there was none.
    """
    reference = str(context.get("tender_reference") or bid.tender_reference)
    codes: list[str] = []  # what the mailbox handed out so far: a used code must not be handed out again

    async def ask_mail(action: dict) -> str:
        task = str(action.get("task") or "").strip()
        if not task:
            return 'ask_mail needs a "task": say what you need from the mailbox and how to recognise it'
        if mail_tab is None:
            return "there is no mailbox in this run, so nothing can be fetched by mail"

        def request() -> str:
            text = f"REQUEST FROM YOUR COLLEAGUE AT THE TENDER PORTAL\n{task}"
            if codes:
                text += ("\n\nANSWERS YOU GAVE EARLIER IN THIS RUN (they are used up: a new request needs a newer "
                         "message)\n" + "\n".join(f"- {code}" for code in codes))
            return text

        system = COURIER.format(site=mail_tab.site_id, url=mail_tab.base_url, reference=reference,
                                actions=ACTIONS_HELP)
        courier = Agent("courier", mail_tab, system, request, deadline=min(deadline, time.time() + MAIL_BUDGET),
                        max_steps=COURIER_STEPS, think=COURIER_THINKS)
        outcome = await courier.run()
        answer = str(outcome.get("answer") or "").strip()
        if not answer:
            return "the mailbox colleague found nothing: " + (outcome.get("summary") or "no result in the time given")
        codes.append(answer)
        return f'the mailbox colleague answers: "{answer}"' + (f' ({outcome["summary"]})' if outcome.get("summary") else "")

    def heading() -> str:
        left = int(deadline - time.time())
        text = f"YOUR JOB: enter, sign and submit the bid for tender {reference}, then read the confirmation."
        if codes:
            text += "\nCodes from the mailbox so far, oldest first: " + ", ".join(codes)
        if left < WRAP_UP:
            text += (f"\nTIME IS SHORT ({left} s). Enter no further positions: leave out the ones not entered yet if "
                     "the form allows it, go straight to the signature, fetch the code and submit what is entered.")
        return text

    bidder = {"company": context.get("company"), "vat_id": context.get("vat_id"), "email": context.get("email")}
    system = CLERK.format(site=tender_tab.site_id, url=tender_tab.base_url, brief=brief, reference=reference,
                          bidder=json.dumps(bidder, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1),
                          sheet=json.dumps(bid_sheet(bid), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), actions=ACTIONS_HELP)
    clerk = Agent("submit", tender_tab, system, heading, extra={"ask_mail": ask_mail}, deadline=deadline,
                  max_steps=CLERK_STEPS, think=CLERK_THINKS)
    outcome = await clerk.run()
    receipt = str(outcome.get("answer") or "").strip()
    notes = str(outcome.get("summary") or "")
    if not outcome.get("done"):
        notes = (notes + " " if notes else "") + f"stopped after {outcome.get('steps', 0)} steps without a confirmation"
    return {"submitted": bool(outcome.get("done") and receipt), "receipt": receipt, "notes": notes}

"""Deterministic bid arithmetic for the RFQ-to-bid challenge.

The agents find and select the evidence; this module only applies the bid rules of the task brief to the structured
facts they filed: exact Decimal arithmetic, ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent, largest-remainder cent allocation, marginal
bonus bands, shared stock and delivery commitments. It contains no scenario values and never touches a website.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP
from fractions import Fraction

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
ZERO = Decimal("0")
HUNDRED = Decimal("100")

# Mass units to grams and index-rate units to EUR per gram, so any combination the sources use multiplies out.
MASS_TO_GRAMS = {"mg": Decimal("0.001"), "g": Decimal(1), "kg": Decimal(1000), "t": Decimal(1000000)}


def round_cents(value) -> Decimal:
    return Decimal(str(value)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def parse_number(raw, number_format: str | None = None) -> Decimal | None:
    """A number as written on a page ("1.234,56", "64,853 (en-US)", 12) as a Decimal; None when there is none.

    `number_format` is "de-DE" (decimal comma) or "en-US" (decimal point); an inline tag in `raw` wins. Without
    either, the separators decide, and a lone comma is read as a decimal comma, as German sources write it.
    """
    if raw is None or isinstance(raw, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(raw, Decimal):
        return raw
    if isinstance(raw, (int, float)):
        return Decimal(str(raw))
    text = str(raw).strip()
    tag = re.search(r"(de-DE|en-US)", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    fmt = (tag.group(1) if tag else number_format or "").lower()
    match = re.search(r"[-+]?\d[\d.,'\s  ]*", text)
    if not match:
        return None
    token = re.sub(r"['\s  ]", "", match.group(0)).rstrip(".,")
    try:
        if fmt == "en-us":
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if fmt == "de-de":
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
        if "," in token and "." in token:
            if token.rfind(",") > token.rfind("."):
                return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if "," in token:
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ".")) if token.count(",") == 1 else Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if token.count(".") > 1:
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", ""))
        return Decimal(token)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def parse_when(raw, end_of_day: bool = False) -> datetime | None:
    """An ISO 8601 date or timestamp (as the extraction step writes them) as an aware UTC datetime.

    A value without a time is a whole day: its start, or its last microsecond with `end_of_day`, so that validity
    periods include both endpoints.
    """
    if not raw:
        return None
    text = str(raw).strip()
    try:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text):
            day = datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return day + timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1) if end_of_day else day
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        german = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\.(\d{4})(?:[,\s]+(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}))?", text)
        if not german:
            return None
        day, month, year, hour, minute = german.groups()
        try:
            when = datetime(int(year), int(month), int(day), int(hour or 0), int(minute or 0))
        except ValueError:
            return None
        if hour is None and end_of_day:
            when += timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1)
    return when.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if when.tzinfo is None else when.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def allocate_cents(total_cents: int, weights: dict[str, Decimal], method: str = "largest_remainder") -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Split `total_cents` across the keys in proportion to `weights`, as EUR amounts that sum exactly.

    Every share is floored to the cent; the cents left over go out by `method`: "largest_remainder" (ties to the
    lower key), "remainder_to_first", "remainder_to_last" or "remainder_to_largest" (the biggest weight).
    """
    keys = sorted(weights, key=position_order)
    total_weight = sum(weights.values(), ZERO)
    if not keys or total_cents <= 0 or total_weight <= 0:
        return {key: ZERO for key in keys}
    # Exact fractions: a tie between remainders must be a tie, not a matter of decimal precision.
    exact = {key: Fraction(total_cents) * Fraction(weights[key]) / Fraction(total_weight) for key in keys}
    cents = {key: math.floor(exact[key]) for key in keys}
    left = total_cents - sum(cents.values())
    if method == "remainder_to_first":
        cents[keys[0]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_last":
        cents[keys[-1]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_largest":
        cents[max(keys, key=lambda key: (weights[key], -keys.index(key)))] += left
    else:
        for key in sorted(keys, key=lambda key: (-(exact[key] - cents[key]), keys.index(key)))[:left]:
            cents[key] += 1
    return {key: Decimal(cents[key]) * CENT for key in keys}


def position_order(key) -> list:
    """Position identifiers in ascending order: their numbers count as numbers ("2" before "10")."""
    return [(0, int(part), "") if part.isdigit() else (1, 0, part) for part in re.findall(r"\d+|\D+", str(key))]


def same_text(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Two attribute values name the same thing: case, spacing and punctuation aside."""
    def norm(value):
        return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zäöüß]+", "", (value or "").lower())
    return norm(a) == norm(b)


NO_CERTIFICATE = ("", "-", "keine", "kein", "ohne", "none", "no", "n/a", "na", "nicht gefordert", "keine gefordert",
                  "nicht erforderlich", "keine erforderlich", "entfällt")


def same_certification(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Certifications match, with every way of writing "none required" counting as the same."""
    def norm(value):
        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (value or "").strip().lower()).strip(" .—–")
        return "" if text in NO_CERTIFICATE else text
    return same_text(norm(a), norm(b))

content.text:
I’m oriented on the project.

QuoteCraft is an agentic solution for Atira’s “RFQ to Bid” challenge:

- Four model-directed browser agents investigate the tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, and mail in parallel.
- Relevant pages become typed evidence in a shared case file.
- A deterministic `Decimal` calculator applies the commercial rules.
- A final agent completes the bid form, retrieves the TAN from mail, and submits.

The architecture and usage are documented in [starter-kit/README.md](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/README.md) and the current handoff is in [PROJECT_STATUS.md](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/PROJECT_STATUS.md).

Key constraint: it must work on unseen/private layouts with no scenario-specific URLs, selectors, credentials, values, or scripted navigation. The model must choose research and navigation at runtime; deterministic code is intentionally limited to browser mechanics, evidence handling, and arithmetic.

Current state: the old hardcoded approach reportedly earned a strong public result but made zero model calls, so it was deliberately replaced. The current model-directed rebuild includes the core agent loop, evidence extraction, 29-rule calculator, submission flow, four-browser configuration, and substantial unit coverage.

Main remaining risks:

- Browser regression: the remote “Load more” collection test is currently failing.
- Question-dialog close state is also documented as unreliable.
- The multi-action submission patch under `tools/` is intentionally not yet applied.
- A public non-submitting end-to-end run and official challenge test still need validation.

I also checked the Entire history: 15 local checkpoints are present on `main`, including the agentic rewrite and test-suite additions. Entire’s remote history search is currently unavailable because this repository is not mirrored to its search service, but the local checkpoints and Brain facts were usable.

QuoteCraft is an agentic solution for Atira’s “RFQ to Bid” challenge:

- Four model-directed browser agents investigate the tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, and mail in parallel.
- Relevant pages become typed evidence in a shared case file.
- A deterministic `Decimal` calculator applies the commercial rules.
- A final agent completes the bid form, retrieves the TAN from mail, and submits.

| Part of QuoteCraft | Main code files | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Overall coordinator | [agent.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.py) | Reads the task, launches the four researcher agents, waits for evidence, calculates the bid, then starts submission. |
| Four browser researchers | [worker.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/worker.py) | Generic model-agent loop used for tender, supplier, ERP, and email sites. The model chooses actions and decides when a page is evidence. |
| Browser interaction | [browser_env.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/browser_env.py) | Converts webpages into accessible text/control descriptions; safely performs click, fill, select, search, page collection, frames, dialogs, and downloads. |
| Model calls | [llm.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/llm.py) | Calls the hosted Qwen model through Atira’s proxy, validates JSON replies, retries failures, and caps concurrency. |
| Shared evidence and facts | [casefile.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/casefile.py) | Stores filed pages, extracts structured tender/ERP/mail facts, merges them, and exposes unanswered research questions. |
| Commercial calculation | [calculator.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/calculator.py) | Pure deterministic `Decimal` bid calculation: material matching, prices, currencies, discounts, stock, delivery, fees, and rounding. |
| Bid entry, TAN, final submission | [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py) | Runs the tender-form clerk agent, asks the mail agent for a fresh TAN, validates form progress, and captures the receipt. |
| Challenge-run plumbing | [run.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/run.py), [browsers.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/browsers.py), [models.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/models.py) | Reads the Atira run contract, connects to the supplied browsers, and provides model configuration. |
| Runtime configuration | [agent.json](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.json) | Declares the setup/run command, Qwen model, and the maximum four browsers. |
| Tests | [tests](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/tests) | Tests calculator rules, agent/submit plumbing, and browser edge cases using local HTML fixtures. |
| Local development helper | [local_run.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/tools/local_run.py) | Runs the system locally against public challenge sites, typically without submitting. |

In short: `agent.py` orchestrates; `worker.py` thinks and researches; `browser_env.py` operates sites; `casefile.py` remembers evidence; `calculator.py` prices; and `submit.py` sends the bid.

I found and checked `maria/build` (the branch name is `maria`, not `mari`).

It is based on `7dce502`, with five Maria-specific commits:

- Faster navigation by disabling model thinking during navigation (`AGENT_THINK=1` re-enables it).
- More resilient mail-gate and extraction timeout handling.
- Retry support when fact extraction fails.
- Optional OpenAI provider for fact extraction via `EXTRACT_PROVIDER`.
- A new `tuning/replay_extraction.py` script for replaying saved evidence against different extraction models.

It changes seven files, primarily [llm.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/llm.py), [casefile.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/casefile.py), [worker.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/worker.py), and its own version of [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py).
